newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei closes at new high for calendar 1997. [CORRECTED 09:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei closes at new high for calendar 1997. [CORRECTED 09:10 GMT]

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index closed at a new high for calendar 1997, boosted by a last-minute spurt in the futures market, brokers said.
They added that stocks had been buoyed throughout the day by small-lot buying amid market talk that pension funds would soon step in to make major purchases.

The Nikkei 225 closed at 20,681.07, up 152.72 points or 0.74 percent. It was the highest close since 20,822.12 posted on December 10. September (corrects from June) Nikkei futures rose 230 points to finish at 20,820.
"Desptite the rise, trade was rather unfocused with purchases seen in a wide variety of issues," said Kunihiro Hatae, Tokyo Securities general manager.

"The Denver Summit and the Bank of Japan's 'tankan' survey are on the horizon and investors were mostly opting for a wait-and-see stance, but they were reluctant to sell as pensions could start buying soon," he added.
